elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Human Capital Index and Tertiary Education Outcomes
elements.content:
Chart type: Two scatter plots side by side comparing Human Capital Index with tertiary education outcomes.

Left Panel: Gross Enrolment Rate at Tertiary Education vs. Human Capital Index
- X-axis: Human Capital Index (range: 0.3 to 0.9)
- Y-axis: Gross Enrolment Rate at Tertiary Education (%) (range: 20 to 100)
- Visual features: Dotted linear trend line running from bottom-left to top-right across the panel; Vietnam (VNM) is highlighted in red, other countries in blue.
- Data points (HCI, GER %):
  - PHL: ≈ (0.54, 36)
  - IDN: ≈ (0.55, 38)
  - THA: ≈ (0.60, 49)
  - MYS: ≈ (0.62, 43)
  - CHN: ≈ (0.65, 50)
  - VNM: ≈ (0.67, 28)
  - KOR: ≈ (0.84, 94)
  - SGP: ≈ (0.88, 84)

Right Panel: Research Output (H-index) vs. Human Capital Index
- X-axis: Human Capital Index (range: 0.3 to 0.9)
- Y-axis: Research Output (H-index) (range: 0 to 1000)
- Visual features: Vietnam (VNM) highlighted with a red dot, other countries shown in green.
- Data points (HCI, H-index):
  - IDN: ≈ (0.54, 200)
  - PHL: ≈ (0.55, 230)
  - THA: ≈ (0.60, 380)
  - MYS: ≈ (0.62, 330)
  - CHN: ≈ (0.65, 830)
  - VNM: ≈ (0.67, 200)
  - KOR: ≈ (0.84, 680)
  - SGP: ≈ (0.88, 560)

Factual comparisons:
- In the left panel, Vietnam (VNM) has a Gross Enrolment Rate of around 28%, which is the lowest among the benchmarked East Asian countries and falls substantially below the regional trend line given its Human Capital Index of ≈ 0.67.
- In the left panel, South Korea (KOR) has the highest tertiary GER (≈ 94%), followed by Singapore (SGP, ≈ 84%).
- In the right panel, China (CHN) achieves the highest research output with an H-index of ≈ 830, while Vietnam (VNM) and Indonesia (IDN) have the lowest at ≈ 200.

Source: HCI data from World Bank (2018a), tertiary GER data from UIS (2018), research output (H-index) data from SCImago (2018).
Note: The data used for the linear trend line for each of the above figures come from a full set of countries with non-missing data. The labels are shown for benchmarking countries from East Asia only. The H-index is a bibliometric index calculated as the maximum number of publications for which each publication is cited at least that many times and thus captures both productivity and impact of research. UIS= UNESCO Institute for Statistics
